column1: # jespersen's own Italian word list (CC0): words respelt as Italian dictionaries write them, for
# what the spelling rules would miss. One per line: the word in lower case, a tab, its respelling.
# A grave accent marks the stress and, on e and o, an open vowel (tàvolo, bène, pòrta); an acute
# one a closed e or o (crédere, sóle); ż is a voiced z (mèżżo); | marks where the words of a compound
# join, so that an s after it keeps its voiceless sound (sta|séra). The rules stress the last syllable
# but one (a final -ai the last: trovai, operai), read -issimo, -abile, -ico, -avano, -arono and
# the like a syllable earlier, open e and o after i and u glides (piède, buòno) and in -ente,
# Stressed three syllables from the end.
# Verbs: infinitives and forms stressed three syllables from the end.
# Open e and o, and closed ones where a rule would open them.
# Stressed i or u before another vowel.
# Voiced z (dz), which the rules give only to a word's first z.
# Compounds whose second word begins with s: it stays voiceless, though between vowels.
